name: pumpfun-token-screening-pipeline
description: Pump.fun Token Screening Pipeline with MCP server/client and RugCheck integration

scripts.build:exe: vite build && tsc && npx @yao-pkg/pkg . --targets host --output dist-exe/pumpfun-sniper-bot.exe
scripts.build:mac: vite build && tsc && npx @yao-pkg/pkg . --targets node22-macos-arm64 --output dist-exe/pumpfun-sniper-bot-macos-arm64
scripts.build:mac-intel: vite build && tsc && npx @yao-pkg/pkg . --targets node22-macos-x64 --output dist-exe/pumpfun-sniper-bot-macos-x64
scripts.test:all: ts-node src/tests/run.ts && ts-node src/tests/filterProofs.ts && ts-node src/tests/guardrailProofs.ts && ts-node src/tests/copySellDrill.ts && ts-node src/tests/copyGasSim.ts

pkg.//assets: NEVER add .env here. pkg embeds assets INSIDE the binary, so bundling .env would bake the builder's HELIUS_API_KEY into every copy of an exe meant to be handed to other people. The key is entered in the UI, read from the environment, or read from a .env placed NEXT TO the exe at runtime.
pkg.//flags: flags.json is deliberately NOT bundled. Bundling it ships whatever the build machine happened to have toggled, so a local experiment leaks into every distributed copy (measured: it shipped allInSizing ON). With no bundled file the binary uses PACKAGED_DEFAULTS, which is explicit and asserted by tests; a user drops their own flags.json beside the exe to override.
pkg.//targets: Windows stays on node18 (its prebuilt base exists and the shipped exe is built from it). macOS uses node22 because there is NO prebuilt node18-macos-arm64 base — pkg 404s and then tries to compile from source. Only the win target is listed here so a bare `pkg .` keeps building the Windows exe; the mac binaries come from build:mac / build:mac-intel, and arm64 must be produced ON macOS (see .github/workflows/release.yml).
